intro_title_en: Start with no Chinese: script and chapter 1 preparation
intro_en: Start here with no Chinese assumed. Read the script preparation for your next chapter before its story. If you arrived through a direct chapter link, use How to read to return here first. The preparation is additional to the chapter, its Pensa and its workbook. You can study it in several short sittings.

Read the Chinese horizontally from left to right. A square written form is a character; a word can contain one or more characters. The story has no spaces between its ordinary words. Punctuation separates clauses and speech. Learn the traditional forms shown here; no simplified-script knowledge is assumed.

Roman letters give modern Mandarin citation readings, not reconstructed ancient sounds. A tone mark belongs to the syllable: ā is high and level, á rises, ǎ dips and rises in isolation, à falls. An unmarked syllable is light. Citation tones may change in connected speech. Keep your tongue as for “ee” and round your lips for ü. Xī'ān has two syllables, xī plus ān; xiān is one syllable. You will answer in Chinese characters, without tone-typing or audio tasks.

For typed answers, a traditional-Chinese pinyin input method lets you type the supplied roman reading without tone marks, then choose the exact written character from its candidates. Compare shapes carefully. While learning input, you can copy a form from the visible reference. Pinyin is a lookup aid; its letters do not all have English sound values, and fluent Mandarin pronunciation is not a prerequisite for following these scenes.

A subject is the person or thing a sentence says something about. In the worked examples a person performs an action on a book: the book is the object directly related to that action. Verbs do not take English-style person or tense endings. No word for “a” or “the” is needed in these examples.

Chapter 1: study only these packets now. Learn each form with its meaning; compare the shapes; try each cue before looking at the answer-check paragraph. Use the reference first, then cover it for another attempt. Answer paragraphs are checks, not extra narrative reading.
Chapter 1, packet 1. New forms:
人 — rén — person.
書 — shū — book; written document.
持 — chí — hold; carry.
取 — qǔ — take.
人持書。 — A person holds a book.
人取書。 — A person takes a book.
Attempt 1. The object being carried is a bound text. Supply its written name: ___ Reference: 人 · 取 · 持 · 書
Attempt 2. Supply the action meaning “take”, rather than keep holding: ___ Reference: 人 · 取 · 持 · 書
Attempt 3. Supply the word for the person, rather than the object carried: ___ Reference: 人 · 取 · 持 · 書
Attempt 4. The book remains in someone’s hands. Supply “hold/carry”: ___ Reference: 人 · 取 · 持 · 書
Attempt 5. From the reference, retrieve the expression for a book rather than a human being: ___ Reference: 人 · 取 · 持 · 書
Attempt 6. The participant who takes the book is a person. Supply that participant word: ___ Reference: 人 · 取 · 持 · 書
Check after attempting: 書 · 取 · 人 · 持 · 書 · 人.
Chapter 1, packet 2. New forms:
安 — Ān — An (novice copyist).
門 — mén — doorway; gate.
入 — rù — enter.
出 — chū — go out.
人 / 入 — These similar strokes join differently. Compare the upper joins and link each form to its own meaning; do not treat them as interchangeable.
Attempt 1. An goes out through the doorway; supply “go out”, not “enter”. 安___門。 Reference: 持 · 出 · 安 · 入 · 取 · 門
Attempt 2. An enters through a doorway; supply the place word. 安入___。 Reference: 持 · 出 · 安 · 入 · 取 · 門
Attempt 3. Choose the expression that means “An (novice copyist)”, then cover the reference and write it: ___ Reference: 持 · 出 · 安 · 入 · 取 · 門
Attempt 4. Write the expression for “enter”; compare it with a different meaning in the reference. ___ Reference: 持 · 出 · 安 · 入 · 取 · 門
Attempt 5. Read the reference in reverse order and retrieve “hold; carry”: ___ Reference: 持 · 出 · 安 · 入 · 取 · 門
Attempt 6. After a brief pause, retrieve “take” from its meaning rather than its place in the list: ___ Reference: 持 · 出 · 安 · 入 · 取 · 門
Check after attempting: 出 · 門 · 安 · 入 · 持 · 取.
Chapter 1, packet 3. New forms:
一 — yī — one.
二 — èr — two.
坐 — zuò — sit.
大 — dà — large.
一 / 二 — Count the separate horizontal strokes: the forms encode different quantities.

In the bounded book-counting examples, the numeral directly precedes the noun: no extra counting word is needed here. Large and small also precede the noun they describe. Broader quantity patterns come later.
Attempt 1. An is seated; supply “sit”, not “stand”. 安___。 Reference: 出 · 一 · 坐 · 二 · 大 · 入
Attempt 2. An carries one book, not two; supply the quantity. 安持___書。 Reference: 出 · 一 · 坐 · 二 · 大 · 入
Attempt 3. Choose the expression that means “two”, then cover the reference and write it: ___ Reference: 出 · 一 · 坐 · 二 · 大 · 入
Attempt 4. Write the expression for “large”; compare it with a different meaning in the reference. ___ Reference: 出 · 一 · 坐 · 二 · 大 · 入
Attempt 5. Read the reference in reverse order and retrieve “enter”: ___ Reference: 出 · 一 · 坐 · 二 · 大 · 入
Attempt 6. After a brief pause, retrieve “go out” from its meaning rather than its place in the list: ___ Reference: 出 · 一 · 坐 · 二 · 大 · 入
Check after attempting: 坐 · 一 · 二 · 大 · 入 · 出.
Chapter 1, packet 4. New forms:
失 — shī — lose.
寧 — Níng — Ning (fellow novice).
小 — xiǎo — small.
得 — dé — obtain.
Attempt 1. Retrieve the written expression for this meaning: “Ning (fellow novice)”. ___ Reference: 坐 · 小 · 得 · 大 · 寧 · 失
Attempt 2. Identify which reference expression has this meaning, without following reference order: “obtain”. ___ Reference: 坐 · 小 · 得 · 大 · 寧 · 失
Attempt 3. Choose the expression that means “lose”, then cover the reference and write it: ___ Reference: 坐 · 小 · 得 · 大 · 寧 · 失
Attempt 4. Ning carries the smaller book; supply “small”, not “large”. 寧持___書。 Reference: 坐 · 小 · 得 · 大 · 寧 · 失
Attempt 5. An carries the larger book; supply “large”, not “small”. 安持___書。 Reference: 坐 · 小 · 得 · 大 · 寧 · 失
Attempt 6. After a brief pause, retrieve “sit” from its meaning rather than its place in the list: ___ Reference: 坐 · 小 · 得 · 大 · 寧 · 失
Check after attempting: 寧 · 得 · 失 · 小 · 大 · 坐.
Chapter 1, packet 5. New forms:
止 — zhǐ — stop.
立 — lì — stand.
行 — xíng — go; travel.
見 — jiàn — see.
Attempt 1. An stops moving; supply “stop”. 安___。 Reference: 大 · 立 · 見 · 止 · 行 · 小
Attempt 2. An is on his feet; supply “stand”, not “sit”. 安___。 Reference: 大 · 立 · 見 · 止 · 行 · 小
Attempt 3. Choose the expression that means “see”, then cover the reference and write it: ___ Reference: 大 · 立 · 見 · 止 · 行 · 小
Attempt 4. Write the expression for “go; travel”; compare it with a different meaning in the reference. ___ Reference: 大 · 立 · 見 · 止 · 行 · 小
Attempt 5. Read the reference in reverse order and retrieve “large”: ___ Reference: 大 · 立 · 見 · 止 · 行 · 小
Attempt 6. After a brief pause, retrieve “small” from its meaning rather than its place in the list: ___ Reference: 大 · 立 · 見 · 止 · 行 · 小
Check after attempting: 止 · 立 · 見 · 行 · 大 · 小.
Chapter 1, packet 6. New forms:
視 — shì — look at.
還 — huán — return.
閉 — bì — close.
開 — kāi — open.
Attempt 1. An opens the doorway; supply “open”, not “close”. 安___門。 Reference: 見 · 還 · 閉 · 視 · 開 · 立
Attempt 2. Identify which reference expression has this meaning, without following reference order: “return”. ___ Reference: 見 · 還 · 閉 · 視 · 開 · 立
Attempt 3. Choose the expression that means “look at”, then cover the reference and write it: ___ Reference: 見 · 還 · 閉 · 視 · 開 · 立
Attempt 4. Ning closes the doorway; supply “close”, not “open”. 寧___門。 Reference: 見 · 還 · 閉 · 視 · 開 · 立
Attempt 5. Read the reference in reverse order and retrieve “stand”: ___ Reference: 見 · 還 · 閉 · 視 · 開 · 立
Attempt 6. After a brief pause, retrieve “see” from its meaning rather than its place in the list: ___ Reference: 見 · 還 · 閉 · 視 · 開 · 立
Check after attempting: 開 · 還 · 視 · 閉 · 立 · 見.

Now read the chapter. Tap an unfamiliar character in the story for its English meaning and contextual reading. Compounds may cover several characters. Reread each scene to follow who acts and who holds each object; a picture is never required to supply a missing meaning.

pensa_hints_en.A: Practise the taught sentence patterns. Read the worked example and its cues before answering.
pensa_hints_en.B: Retrieve words in meaningful sentences. The bank has extra words; do not use every word.
pensa_hints_en.C: Answer the scene cues in your own Chinese sentences, in story order. Then compare with the models; yes/no and isolated names do not answer these tasks.
